claim: cite
rationale: Nesting and the "Derives from:" line are the two ways a unit says what it follows from. A unit [sits in](#term-sit) or [derives from](#term-derive) what it cites. A [link](#term-link) in the body is neither.
formula: pred cites[u, v: Unit] { u->v in Sit.rel or u->v in Derive.rel }

claim: unfounded
rationale: A unit that lacks a citation its kind owes: what it follows from.

claim: miscited
rationale: A unit that cites a kind of unit it may not cite. A conflict names the units it sets against each other on a line of its own, which is no citation.
formula:
pred miscited[u: Unit] {
  (u in Axiom and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v] and v not in Axiom))
  or (u in Fact and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v]))
  or (u in Spec and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v] and v not in Axiom and v not in Spec and v not in Fact))
  or (u in Exception and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v] and v not in Spec and v not in Fact))
  or (u in Bug and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v] and v not in Spec))
  or (u in Conflict and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v]))
  or (u in Term and (some v: Unit | cites[u, v]))
}

claim: circular
rationale: A unit that follows from itself: it cites a unit that [depends](#term-depend) on it, and that unit may be the unit itself. A unit that cites itself is a loop of one, and a unit whose citations lead back to it is a longer loop.
formula: pred circular[u: Unit] { some v: Unit | cites[u, v] and v->u in Depend.rel }

claim: refined
rationale: A bug that sits in a spec marks where the code breaks the spec. It refines nothing, so a spec that holds only bugs is a leaf.
formula: pred refined[c: Claim] { (some s: Spec | s->c in Sit.rel) or (some e: Exception | e->c in Sit.rel) }

claim: unguarded
rationale: A leaf that no test checks: the code can stop doing what it says, and no test fails.
formula: pred unguarded[c: Claim] { not refined[c] and not tested[c] }

claim: adrift
rationale: A test whose tags do not say which leaf it checks.

claim: used
rationale: A unit that nothing uses can stop being true, and nothing that relies on it notices, because nothing does.

claim: check
rationale: A test checks the units its tags name. That is no citation: [citing](#term-cite) is what one unit does to another.
formula: pred checks[t: Test, u: Unit] { some g: Tag | t->g in Carry.rel and g->u in Name.tag }

claim: tested
rationale: A test of a bug asserts what the spec the bug breaks claims, so it tests that spec too. A plain test that checks a bug still makes the bug tested: the checker reports the test instead, as [misleading](#term-misleading).

claim: paired
rationale: A conflict needs two sides.
formula: pred paired[c: Conflict] { some a, b: Unit | a != b and c->a in Name.between and c->b in Name.between }

claim: hidden
rationale: A known defect out of sight: no open issue tracks it, no test checks it, or a conflict that does not say which units it sets against each other. A project with no [tracker](#term-tracker) owes no issue, and a project with no [runner](#term-runner) owes no test.

claim: misleading
rationale: A test whose outcome says nothing true about a defect: an expected failure that names no defect, or a test that passes while the bug it checks is there.

claim: list
formula: pred lists[f: Frontmatter, p: Plugin] { some e: Entry | f->e in Item.rel and e->p in Spell.rel }

claim: apply
formula: pred applies[p: Plugin, d: Document] { some f: Listing | d->f in Head.rel and lists[f, p] }

claim: call
availability
every claim says what it follows from
rationale: A claim that cannot say why it holds gives the next reader no reason to keep it, or to change it with care. So a canon passes the check only when every claim [cites](#term-cite) what it follows from, and only what its kind may follow from. A unit that does not is [unfounded](#term-unfounded) or [miscited](#term-miscited), and the checker reports a [finding](#term-finding) for it. A claim that follows from itself says no more than that it holds. A unit that is [circular](#term-circular) has a finding as well.
formula:
(all u: Unit | unfounded[u] implies u in Finding)
and (all u: Unit | miscited[u] implies u in Finding)
and (all u: Unit | circular[u] implies u in Finding)

claim: an unfounded unit is freelancing
rationale: This follows because a [freelancing](#term-freelancing) is the finding for a claim that cites nothing it follows from.
formula: all u: Unit | unfounded[u] implies u in Freelancing
parents: every claim says what it follows from

claim: a spec cites an axiom or a spec
formula: all s: Spec | ((no a: Axiom | cites[s, a]) and (no t: Spec | cites[s, t])) implies s in Freelancing
parents: every claim says what it follows from
an unfounded unit is freelancing

claim: an exception cites a spec
formula: all e: Exception | (no s: Spec | cites[e, s]) implies e in Freelancing
parents: every claim says what it follows from
an unfounded unit is freelancing

claim: an exception cites a fact
formula: all e: Exception | (no f: Fact | cites[e, f]) implies e in Freelancing
parents: every claim says what it follows from
an unfounded unit is freelancing

claim: a bug cites a spec
formula: all b: Bug | (no s: Spec | cites[b, s]) implies b in Freelancing
parents: every claim says what it follows from
an unfounded unit is freelancing

claim: a miscited unit is misnested
rationale: This follows because a [misnesting](#term-misnesting) is the finding for a unit that cites a kind it may not cite.
formula: all u: Unit | miscited[u] implies u in Misnesting
parents: every claim says what it follows from

claim: an axiom cites only axioms
formula: all a: Axiom | (some u: Unit | cites[a, u] and u not in Axiom) implies a in Misnesting
parents: every claim says what it follows from
a miscited unit is misnested

claim: a fact cites nothing
formula: all f: Fact | (some u: Unit | cites[f, u]) implies f in Misnesting
parents: every claim says what it follows from
a miscited unit is misnested

claim: a spec cites only axioms specs and facts
formula: all s: Spec | (some u: Unit | cites[s, u] and u not in Axiom and u not in Spec and u not in Fact) implies s in Misnesting
parents: every claim says what it follows from
a miscited unit is misnested

claim: an exception cites only specs and facts
formula: all e: Exception | (some u: Unit | cites[e, u] and u not in Spec and u not in Fact) implies e in Misnesting
parents: every claim says what it follows from
a miscited unit is misnested

claim: a bug cites only specs
formula: all b: Bug | (some u: Unit | cites[b, u] and u not in Spec) implies b in Misnesting
parents: every claim says what it follows from
a miscited unit is misnested

claim: a conflict cites nothing
formula: all c: Conflict | (some u: Unit | cites[c, u]) implies c in Misnesting
parents: every claim says what it follows from
a miscited unit is misnested

claim: a term cites nothing
formula: all t: Term | (some u: Unit | cites[t, u]) implies t in Misnesting
parents: every claim says what it follows from
a miscited unit is misnested

claim: a unit does not depend on itself
rationale: This follows because a unit that [depends](#term-depend) on itself names no ground it stands on, and a [cycle](#term-cycle) is its finding.
formula: all u: Unit | circular[u] implies u in Cycle
parents: every claim says what it follows from

claim: a known defect stays in sight
rationale: A defect the canon knows of must stay where the next reader sees it, until it is fixed or the owner of the design rules on it. A bug or a conflict out of sight is [hidden](#term-hidden), and a [test](#term-test) whose outcome says nothing true about a defect is [misleading](#term-misleading). The checker reports a [finding](#term-finding) for each.
formula:
(all b: Bug | hidden[b] implies b in Finding)
and (all c: Conflict | hidden[c] implies c in Finding)
and (all t: Test | misleading[t] implies t in Finding)

claim: a hidden bug is reported
rationale: This follows because each way a bug is hidden has a finding of its own. A bug that [names](#term-name) no [issue](#term-issue) has an [untracking](#term-untracking), and one that names an issue the [tracker](#term-tracker) does not know has a [mistracking](#term-mistracking). One that names an issue the tracker has closed has an [outdated tracking](#term-outdated-tracking), and one that is not [tested](#term-tested) has an [untesting](#term-untesting).
formula: all b: Bug | hidden[b] implies b in Finding
parents: a known defect stays in sight

claim: a bug names an issue
formula: all b: Bug | (some Tracker and (no i: Issue | b->i in Name.issue)) implies b in Untracking
parents: a known defect stays in sight
a hidden bug is reported

claim: a bug names an issue the tracker knows
formula: all b: Bug | (some i: Issue | b->i in Name.issue and i not in Known) implies b in Mistracking
parents: a known defect stays in sight
a hidden bug is reported

claim: a bug names an open issue
formula: all b: Bug | (some i: Issue | b->i in Name.issue and i in Closed) implies b in OutdatedTracking
parents: a known defect stays in sight
a hidden bug is reported

claim: a bug is tested
formula: all b: Bug | (some Runner and not tested[b]) implies b in Untesting
parents: a known defect stays in sight
a hidden bug is reported

claim: a hidden conflict is reported
rationale: This follows because each way a conflict is hidden has a finding of its own: the same three as a bug's for its issue, and an [unpairing](#term-unpairing) when it is not [paired](#term-paired).
formula: all c: Conflict | hidden[c] implies c in Finding
parents: a known defect stays in sight

claim: a conflict names an issue
formula: all c: Conflict | (some Tracker and (no i: Issue | c->i in Name.issue)) implies c in Untracking
parents: a known defect stays in sight
a hidden conflict is reported

claim: a conflict names an issue the tracker knows
formula: all c: Conflict | (some i: Issue | c->i in Name.issue and i not in Known) implies c in Mistracking
parents: a known defect stays in sight
a hidden conflict is reported

claim: a conflict names an open issue
formula: all c: Conflict | (some i: Issue | c->i in Name.issue and i in Closed) implies c in OutdatedTracking
parents: a known defect stays in sight
a hidden conflict is reported

claim: a conflict names two units
formula: all c: Conflict | not paired[c] implies c in Unpairing
parents: a known defect stays in sight
a hidden conflict is reported

claim: a misleading test is reported
rationale: This follows because each way a test is misleading has a finding of its own. An [expected failure](#term-expected-failure) that [checks](#term-check) no bug and no exception has an [unexplained failure](#term-unexplained-failure), and a [plain test](#term-plain-test) that checks a bug has an [unpinning](#term-unpinning).
formula: all t: Test | misleading[t] implies t in Finding
parents: a known defect stays in sight

claim: an expected failure checks a bug or an exception
formula: all x: ExpectedFailure | ((no b: Bug | checks[x, b]) and (no e: Exception | checks[x, e])) implies x in UnexplainedFailure
parents: a known defect stays in sight
a misleading test is reported

claim: a plain test does not check a bug
formula: all t: PlainTest | (some b: Bug | checks[t, b]) implies t in Unpinning
parents: a known defect stays in sight
a misleading test is reported

claim: a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed
rationale: This narrows taking the check at its word to a clean check: when the checker reports nothing, the canon has not gone out of date. Documentation goes out of date because nothing checks it. A canon goes out of date unnoticed when a claim no test checks stops holding, or when a test stops saying which claim it checks. It goes out of date as well when a link no longer leads where it says. So every leaf claim is [tested](#term-tested), and every [test](#term-test) [checks](#term-check) a leaf through its [tags](#term-tag). A claim that is not is [unguarded](#term-unguarded), and a test that does not is [adrift](#term-adrift). A project with no [runner](#term-runner) has no tests, and holds its canon to itself alone: it owes no test. So too every [pointer](#term-pointer), [index](#term-index) and [site](#term-site) leads where it says, and every id names one unit.
formula:
(all c: Claim | (some Runner and unguarded[c]) implies c in Finding)
and (all g: Tag | (no u: Unit | g->u in Name.tag) implies g in Finding)
and (all t: Test | adrift[t] implies t in Finding)
and (all p: Pointer | (no x: Target | p->x in Name.pointer) implies p in Finding)
and (all u: Unit | (not used[u] and u not in Conflict) implies u in Finding)
and (all u: Unit | (some t: Trailer | t->u in Follow.rel) implies u in Finding)
and (all d: Document | ((some u: Unit | d->u in Hold.units) and (no i: Index | d->i in Hold.indexes)) implies d in Finding)
and (all d: Document | (some i: Index | d->i in Hold.indexes and i->d not in Match.rel) implies d in Finding)
and (all c: Claim | (some s: Site | c->s in Name.site and (no r: Source | r->s in Hold.symbols)) implies c in Finding)
and (all u: Unit | (some v: Unit | u->v in Repeat.rel) implies u in Finding)
parents: the check can be taken at its word

claim: an unguarded claim is untested
rationale: This follows because an [untesting](#term-untesting) is the finding for a leaf that no test checks.
formula: all c: Claim | (some Runner and unguarded[c]) implies c in Untesting
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed

claim: a tag names a unit
rationale: This follows because a tag that names no unit checks nothing, and a [rotting](#term-rotting) is its finding. A tag rots when the unit it names is renamed or removed.
formula: all g: Tag | (no u: Unit | g->u in Name.tag) implies g in Rotting
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed

claim: an adrift test is reported
rationale: This follows because each way a test is adrift has a finding of its own. A test that [project](#term-project) [declares](#term-declare) has an [uncitation](#term-uncitation) when it [carries](#term-carry) no tag. It has a [misaiming](#term-misaiming) when it checks a unit that is no [claim](#term-claim). A test that checks a [refined](#term-refined) claim has an [overreach](#term-overreach).
formula: all t: Test | adrift[t] implies t in Finding
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed

claim: a declared test carries a tag
formula: all t: Test | (t in Declared and (no g: Tag | t->g in Carry.rel)) implies t in Uncitation
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed
an adrift test is reported

claim: a declared test checks only claims
formula: all t: Test | (t in Declared and (some u: Unit | checks[t, u] and u not in Claim)) implies t in Misaiming
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed
an adrift test is reported

claim: a test checks only leaves
formula: all t: Test | (some c: Claim | checks[t, c] and refined[c]) implies t in Overreach
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed
an adrift test is reported

claim: a pointer names a target
rationale: This follows because a pointer that names no [target](#term-target) leads nowhere, and a [rotting](#term-rotting) is its finding. A pointer rots when the file or the unit it names is renamed or removed.
formula: all p: Pointer | (no x: Target | p->x in Name.pointer) implies p in Rotting
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed

claim: a unit is declared once
rationale: This follows because a unit that [repeats](#term-repeat) another shares its id, so no pointer or tag can say which of the two it names.
formula: all u: Unit | (some v: Unit | u->v in Repeat.rel) implies u in Rotting
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed

claim: a unit is used
rationale: This follows because a unit nothing [uses](#term-used) can go out of date, and nothing that relies on it notices. An [orphaning](#term-orphaning) is its finding. A conflict is no part of the theory, only a record of where it fails, so nothing uses it.
formula: all u: Unit | (not used[u] and u not in Conflict) implies u in Orphaning
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed

claim: a heading ends with its id
rationale: This follows because a [trailer](#term-trailer) changes the anchor the page renders, so a pointer to the unit's id leads nowhere on the page. A [misanchoring](#term-misanchoring) is its finding.
formula: all u: Unit | (some t: Trailer | t->u in Follow.rel) implies u in Misanchoring
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed

claim: a document holds an index
rationale: This follows because a [document](#term-document) with units and no [index](#term-index) has no generated list to check, and a [misindexing](#term-misindexing) is its finding.
formula: all d: Document | ((some u: Unit | d->u in Hold.units) and (no i: Index | d->i in Hold.indexes)) implies d in Misindexing
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed

claim: an index matches its document
rationale: This follows because an index that does not [match](#term-match) its document lists units or statements that are no longer there.
formula: all d: Document | (some i: Index | d->i in Hold.indexes and i->d not in Match.rel) implies d in Misindexing
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed

claim: a site is held by a source
rationale: This follows because a [site](#term-site) that no [source](#term-source) [holds](#term-hold) was renamed or removed, and a [mislocation](#term-mislocation) is its finding.
formula: all c: Claim | (some s: Site | c->s in Name.site and (no r: Source | r->s in Hold.symbols)) implies c in Mislocation
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed

claim: a document is context for the documents that extend it and for theirs
rationale: This follows because a document that extends another takes in what that one takes in, and the author does not list it again.
formula: all d: Document, e: Document, g: Document | (d->e in Extend.rel implies d->e in Context.rel) and ((d->e in Extend.rel and e->g in Context.rel) implies d->g in Context.rel)
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed

claim: a fenced block with a language belongs to the unit whose own text holds it
rationale: This follows because the logic of a unit is what its own text holds. The statement of the unit says that logic and no other.
formula: all f: Fence, u: Unit | (f in Languaged and f->u in Within.rel) implies u->f in Blocks.rel
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed

claim: a fence with no language is prose
rationale: This follows because a fence with no language shows text, and no backend can check it.
formula: all f: Fence | f not in Languaged implies (no u: Unit | u->f in Blocks.rel)
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed

claim: a block whose second word is vocabulary has the role of vocabulary
rationale: This follows because the author states what a block is for in the second word, and the checker reads no other sign.
formula: all f: Fence | f in VocabularyWord implies f in VocabularyBlock
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed

claim: a block whose second word is bounds has the role of bounds
rationale: This follows because the second word is the one sign of the role.
formula: all f: Fence | f in BoundsWord implies f in BoundsBlock
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed

claim: a block whose second word is scenario has the role of scenario
rationale: This follows because the second word is the one sign of the role.
formula: all f: Fence | f in ScenarioWord implies f in ScenarioBlock
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed

claim: a block with no role word is the formula of its unit
rationale: This follows because most blocks are the formula of the unit, and the author need not write a word for the common case.
formula: all f: Fence | f in NoSecondWord implies f in UnitBlock
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed

claim: a nested units block is its own
rationale: This follows because a unit nested in another says its own logic. The unit above does not say it.
formula: all f: Fence, u: Unit | f->u in Within.rel implies (no v: Unit | v->u in Sit.rel and v->f in Blocks.rel)
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a canon cannot go out of date unnoticed

claim: a tested claim is not untested
rationale: This follows because an [untesting](#term-untesting) says that no test checks a claim, and for a [tested](#term-tested) claim that is false.
formula: all c: Claim | tested[c] implies c not in Untesting
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a finding is never false

claim: a claim a declared test checks is not untested
rationale: This follows because a test that the project [declares](#term-declare) checks the units its tags name.
formula: all c: Claim | (some t: Test | t in Declared and checks[t, c]) implies c not in Untesting
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a finding is never false
a tested claim is not untested

claim: a claim an undeclared test checks is not untested
rationale: This follows because a test checks the units its tags name, in whatever file of the sources it sits. That file can be a suite the project does not declare. It can also be a module that builds tests from a table of cases, which a suite then runs. The tags of such a test are as true as the tags of a test in a declared suite.
formula: all c: Claim | (some t: Test | t not in Declared and checks[t, c]) implies c not in Untesting
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a finding is never false
a tested claim is not untested

claim: a spec whose bug a test checks is not untested
rationale: This follows because a test of a [bug](#term-bug) asserts what the spec the bug sits in claims.
formula: all s: Spec | (some t: Test, b: Bug | checks[t, b] and b->s in Sit.rel) implies s not in Untesting
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a finding is never false
a tested claim is not untested

claim: a project with no runner reports no untesting
rationale: This follows because a test is a call that a [runner](#term-runner) declares, so a project with no runner has no tests. An [untesting](#term-untesting) there would ask for a test that the project has chosen not to have.
formula: all u: Unit | no Runner implies u not in Untesting
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a finding is never false

claim: a project with no tracker reports no untracking
rationale: This follows because an [issue](#term-issue) is an entry of the [tracker](#term-tracker). A project with no tracker has no issue that a bug or a conflict could name. An [untracking](#term-untracking) there would ask for an issue line that names nothing, which an author could only meet with a number that tracks no work.
formula: all u: Unit | no Tracker implies u not in Untracking
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a finding is never false

claim: a check the project asked for is never dropped silently
rationale: This narrows taking the check at its word to the checks the project asks for: a check that did not run never passes for clean. A project asks for its checks in its documents: the plugins a document names, and the command it runs. A check that the project asks for either runs, or the author hears that it could not. Otherwise a mistake as small as a misspelled key turns a check off, and the author trusts a canon that nothing has checked. So a [run](#term-run) that asks for what the checker cannot deliver exits with code 2. Code 2 stands above a finding and above success. Four things ask for too much. One is a [plugin](#term-plugin) the project lacks. Another is a [frontmatter](#term-frontmatter) the checker cannot read. The others are a [command](#term-command) that nothing adds, and a plugin that could not run.
formula: all r: Run | ((some f: Frontmatter, p: Missing | lists[f, p]) or (some d: Document | d in Unreadable) or (some c: Command | r->c in Ask.rel and not available[c]) or (some p: Plugin | r->p in Return.code2)) implies r in Exits2
parents: the check can be taken at its word

claim: a document gets the plugins it asks for
rationale: This follows because the plugins a document names are the checks it asks for. It gets those and no others. A plugin it did not ask for adds no finding, and one it asked for is not left out. A document that names none asks for none.
formula: all p: Plugin, d: Document | (applies[p, d] implies p->d in Over.rel) and ((d not in Given and p->d in Over.rel) implies applies[p, d])
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a check the project asked for is never dropped silently

claim: a document with no plugins list asks for no plugin
rationale: This follows because such a document names no plugin, so it asks for no check.
formula: all p: Plugin, d: Document | ((no f: Listing | d->f in Head.rel) and d not in Given) implies p->d not in Over.rel
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a check the project asked for is never dropped silently
a document gets the plugins it asks for

claim: a plugin a document lists runs over it
rationale: This follows because a plugin that is listed is asked for.
formula: all p: Plugin, d: Document, f: Listing | (d->f in Head.rel and lists[f, p]) implies p->d in Over.rel
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a check the project asked for is never dropped silently
a document gets the plugins it asks for

claim: a plugin a document does not list does not run over it
rationale: This follows because a list is the whole of what the document asks for.
formula: all p: Plugin, d: Document, f: Listing | (d->f in Head.rel and not lists[f, p] and d not in Given) implies p->d not in Over.rel
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a check the project asked for is never dropped silently
a document gets the plugins it asks for

claim: an empty list asks for no plugin
rationale: This follows because an empty list is an answer: the document asks for no plugin, and the commands of the checker are still there.
formula: all p: Plugin, d: Document, f: Listing | (d->f in Head.rel and (no e: Entry | f->e in Item.rel) and d not in Given) implies p->d not in Over.rel
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a check the project asked for is never dropped silently
a document gets the plugins it asks for

claim: a document named on the command line is checked whatever its frontmatter says
rationale: This follows because naming a file on the command line asks for the check of that file.
formula: all r: Run, p: Plugin, d: Given | calls[r, p] implies p->d in Over.rel
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a check the project asked for is never dropped silently
a document gets the plugins it asks for

claim: a frontmatter with no plugins key holds no entry
rationale: This follows because a block with no key asks for nothing, and so the document names no plugin.
formula: all f: Frontmatter | f not in Listing implies (no e: Entry | f->e in Item.rel)
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a check the project asked for is never dropped silently
a frontmatter lists what is written in it

claim: a flawed frontmatter is refused
rationale: This follows because the checker reads a small part of YAML and nothing else. A block it misreads would drop a check without a word, so it refuses a block with a flaw.
formula: all f: Frontmatter | (f in Misquoted or f in Foreign or f in Unclosed or f in Unterminated or f in Doubled or f in Dangling or f in Looping or f in Stray) implies f in Refused
parents: the check can be taken at its word
a check the project asked for is never dropped silently

claim: a misquoted entry is refused
rationale: This follows because YAML does not read an unquoted entry with an at sign as a package name, and the author meant the package.
formula: all f: Misquoted | f in Refused

claim: a statement says what its logic says
rationale: A reader of the canon learns what a unit claims from its statement. If a person writes the statement apart from the logic, the two drift, and the reader learns what the logic does not hold. So the checker says the statement of a unit that holds a formula from that formula, in the same words each time, with [naturalloy](../naturalloy/CANON.md#axiom-a-formula-is-said-without-loss). It reports a statement that is not what the formula says. The words of the statements are the words of the logic. A reading of a word that nothing declares, or a word declared out of place, would let a statement say what the logic does not.

claim: the claims of a canon never contradict each other
rationale: Every claim of a canon says how the project is, and the claims are about one project. If two of them cannot both hold, the canon says nothing. A reader cannot follow both, and a change that obeys one breaks the other. The same goes for a situation that the canon says must be possible and that one of its claims rules out. So the checker asks the analyzer two things. Can the claims hold together? Can each scenario happen? It names the units that a repair has to touch.
formula: (all u: Unit | u in Contradicting implies u in Named) and (all c: Scenario | c in Impossible implies c in Raised)

claim: a formula with no keyword is a claim to hold
rationale: This follows because a unit that states a bare formula states a claim, and the analyzer must hold the claim to find a contradiction.
formula: all u: Unit | u in BareFormula implies u in Held
parents: the claims of a canon never contradict each other

claim: the first searches leave no unit out
rationale: This follows because the author learns first whether the canon holds together, and the searches that leave a unit out cost much more.
formula: all s: Search | s in First implies s not in Trial
parents: the claims of a canon never contradict each other

claim: a trial is made only for a scenario that cannot happen

formula: all s: Search, c: Scenario | (s in Trial and s->c in Pose.scenario) implies (c in Impossible and s in Afterwards)

claim: a trial leaves out one held unit and keeps the rest

formula: all s: Search, c: Scenario, u: Unit | (s in Trial and s->c in Pose.scenario and s->u in Leave.rel and (some v: Unit | c->v in Probe.rel)) implies c->u in Probe.rel
parents: the claims of a canon never contradict each other

claim: the claims of an extended document join the model

claim: a formula can be held against the other formulas
rationale: A reader takes a unit with a formula as checked. The analyzer holds its formula against the other formulas, and would find a contradiction between them. That holds only when something else in the model speaks of the words the formula uses. A formula that no other formula can contradict holds whatever the rest of the canon says. It looks checked and is not, and the reader trusts a claim that nothing has checked. So the checker reports a formula that no other formula can contradict, and only such a formula. It finds one by the signatures it is [lone](#term-lone-formula) on. The author can tie the signature to the rest of the model, with a definition, a fact or a scenario that names it. Or the author can take the formula away and write the statement of the unit by hand, so that the unit no longer looks checked. Then its test guards it.
formula: (all u: Unit | (u in Logical and u not in Term and u in Unchallenged) implies (some w: Signature | u->w in Expose.rel)) and (all u: Unit, w: Word | u->w in Expose.rel implies u in Unchallenged)

claim: a formula that no other formula can contradict is reported

formula: all u: Unit | (u in Logical and u not in Term and u in Unchallenged) implies (some w: Signature | u->w in Expose.rel)
parents: a formula can be held against the other formulas

claim: a formula that is lone on a signature is reported

formula: all u: Unit, w: Signature | (u in Logical and u not in Term and loneOn[u, w]) implies u->w in Expose.rel
parents: a formula can be held against the other formulas

a formula is reported only when no other formula can contradict it

claim: a signature that another unit names keeps a formula from being reported
rationale: This follows because the other unit constrains the signature, so it can contradict the formula.
formula: all u: Unit, v: Unit, w: Word | (v != u and v->w in Utter.rel) implies u->w not in Expose.rel
parents: a formula can be held against the other formulas
a formula is reported only when no other formula can contradict it
a formula is reported only on a signature it is lone on

claim: a signature that a scenario names keeps a formula from being reported
rationale: This follows because the analyzer reports a scenario that the formula rules out. So the scenario holds the formula against something, even in the unit of the formula.
formula: all u: Unit, v: Unit, w: Word | v->w in Picture.rel implies u->w not in Expose.rel
parents: a formula can be held against the other formulas
a formula is reported only when no other formula can contradict it
a formula is reported only on a signature it is lone on

claim: a signature that an extended document names keeps a formula from being reported
rationale: This follows because the claims of an extended document join the model, so they can contradict the formula.
formula: all d: Document, e: Document, u: Unit, v: Unit, w: Word | (d->e in Context.rel and d->u in Hold.units and e->v in Hold.units and v->w in Utter.rel) implies u->w not in Expose.rel
parents: a formula can be held against the other formulas
a formula is reported only when no other formula can contradict it
a formula is reported only on a signature it is lone on

claim: a formula is not reported on a field or a predicate
rationale: This follows because a predicate has a body that ties it to the other words. The check leaves fields out for now. It reads a field by its name, and two signatures can give a field the same name.
formula: all u: Unit, w: Word | w not in Signature implies u->w not in Expose.rel

claim: a term is not reported as lone
rationale: This follows because a term gives a word its meaning and claims nothing.
formula: all u: Term, w: Word | u->w not in Expose.rel

claim: a document that keeps no readings has no formula reported as lone
rationale: This follows because the check of lone formulas is part of the check of words, which reads only a document that keeps readings.
formula: all d: Document, u: Unit, w: Word | (d not in Worded and d->u in Hold.units) implies u->w not in Expose.rel

claim: a lone formula fails check
rationale: This follows because a formula that looks checked and is not must not let the check succeed.
formula: all r: Run, c: CheckCommand, u: Unit, w: Word | (r->c in Ask.rel and u->w in Expose.rel) implies r not in Exits0

claim: fit
formula: pred fits[f: Quantifier] { f not in VariableTwice and f not in NothingToAttach and f not in NoWithAnother and f not in ConditionAside and f not in TimedCondition }

claim: by kind
formula: pred byKind[d: Definition] { d not in NoKindFirst and d not in AmbiguousAnd and d not in NotAboutSubject }

claim: sentenceable
formula: pred sentenceable[f: Series] { f in Few and f not in NotClause and (f not in CommaItem or f not in MoreThanTwo) and f not in TooLong and f not in TimeBeforeLast and f not in RelativeBeforeLast }

claim: a rule of two clauses is said on one line
rationale: This follows because a short rule is clearest as one sentence, "when this, that".
formula: all f: Series | (f in OneLineRule and f not in TimeFirst) implies f in OneLine
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: a definition by cases is said as a noun phrase for each kind
rationale: This follows because a reader takes in "a spec that cites no axiom" faster than a sentence about a unit that is a spec. The phrase says the same in fewer words.
formula: all f: Definition | (f in GuardedByKind and byKind[f]) implies f in PhrasePerKind
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: the alternatives of one kind are put together with or
rationale: This follows because two alternatives for one kind are two ways to be that kind, and one phrase says so.
formula: all f: Definition | (f in SameKindTwice and byKind[f]) implies f in JoinedWithOr
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: the options of an or inside a kind are one coordination
rationale: This follows because options in one kind read as one run of "names, names or is".
formula: all f: Definition | (f in OrInsideKind and byKind[f]) implies f in OneCoordination
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: a definition with one kind is one sentence
rationale: This follows because a list of one line is no list.
formula: all f: Definition | (f in OneKind and byKind[f]) implies f in OneSentenceKind
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: a definition by cases is said as it stands when an alternative does not begin with its kind
rationale: This follows because a phrase for a kind needs the kind first, and an alternative without it would lose what it says.
formula: all f: Definition | f in NoKindFirst implies f in AsItStands
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: a definition by cases is said as it stands when a run of and would read two ways
rationale: This follows because a run of and beside another alternative of its kind could join to either, and the reader should not guess.
formula: all f: Definition | f in AmbiguousAnd implies f in AsItStands
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: a definition by cases is said as it stands when an alternative is not about its subject
rationale: This follows because a phrase for a kind is about the subject, and an alternative about something else would get the wrong words.
formula: all f: Definition | f in NotAboutSubject implies f in AsItStands
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: a variable said once takes the place of its quantifier as a noun phrase
rationale: This follows because "sits in no unit" is one phrase. Spelled out with a numbered name, it takes twice the words.
formula: all f: Quantifier | (f in VariableOnce and fits[f]) implies f in AsNounPhrase
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: a noun phrase can be the subject of a sentence
rationale: This follows because the thing the sentence is about may be the variable.
formula: all f: Quantifier | (f in VariableSubject and fits[f]) implies f in AsSubjectPhrase
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: what else is true of the variable is a relative clause
rationale: This follows because a condition on the variable is a part of the phrase that names it.
formula: all f: Quantifier | (f in VariableWithCondition and fits[f]) implies f in RelativeClause
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: a quantifier whose variable would be said twice is said in full
rationale: This follows because a phrase that says the variable in two places would hide that it is one thing.
formula: all f: Quantifier | f in VariableTwice implies f in InFull
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: a quantifier with nothing to attach to is said in full
rationale: This follows because a phrase needs a place in the sentence, and a variable beside nothing else has none.
formula: all f: Quantifier | f in NothingToAttach implies f in InFull
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: no with another is said in full
rationale: This follows because "no" with "another" in one phrase would mean something else than the logic says, so the verbalizer spells it out.
formula: all f: Quantifier | f in NoWithAnother implies f in InFull
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: a quantifier with a time phrase in one of several conditions is said in full
rationale: This follows because a time phrase in a noun phrase would cover the other conditions too, where the formula has it cover one.
formula: all f: Quantifier | f in TimedCondition implies f in InFull
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: a condition that is not about the variable is said in full
rationale: This follows because the phrase would put the condition in the wrong place.
formula: all f: Quantifier | f in ConditionAside implies f in InFull
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: three clauses or fewer are said in a sentence
rationale: This follows because a short list in a sentence is easier to read than bullets.
formula: all f: Series | sentenceable[f] implies f in AsSentence
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: a longer list or a list with a comma is bullets
rationale: This follows because a sentence of many conditions loses the reader, and so does one with commas or items of more than a clause.
formula: all f: Series | (f in Items and not sentenceable[f]) implies f in AsBullets
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: a list of more than three clauses is bullets
rationale: This follows because a sentence of four conditions loses the reader.
formula: all f: Series | f in Many implies f in AsBullets
parents: a formula is said without loss
a longer list or a list with a comma is bullets

claim: a list with a comma in an item and more than two clauses is bullets
rationale: This follows because a comma inside an item makes a list of three read as a list of more.
formula: all f: Series | (f in CommaItem and f in MoreThanTwo) implies f in AsBullets
parents: a formula is said without loss
a longer list or a list with a comma is bullets

claim: a list too long for a line is bullets
rationale: This follows because a sentence that runs past a line is hard to take in at once.
formula: all f: Series | f in TooLong implies f in AsBullets
parents: a formula is said without loss
a longer list or a list with a comma is bullets

claim: a list with a time phrase before its last clause is bullets
rationale: This follows because a time phrase at the start of a sentence reads as covering each clause after it. The formula has it cover one.
formula: all f: Series | f in TimeBeforeLast implies f in AsBullets
parents: a formula is said without loss
a longer list or a list with a comma is bullets

claim: a list with a relative clause before its last clause is bullets
rationale: This follows because a relative clause can run on over the clauses after it. "An owner that pulse has disposed and code has registered c" reads so. The formula ends it with its own clause.
formula: all f: Series | f in RelativeBeforeLast implies f in AsBullets
parents: a formula is said without loss
a longer list or a list with a comma is bullets

claim: an item that is more than a clause makes the list bullets
rationale: This follows because an item with a quantifier or a list of its own cannot stand in a sentence beside others.
formula: all f: Series | f in NotClause implies f in AsBullets
parents: a formula is said without loss
a longer list or a list with a comma is bullets

claim: an and inside an or is kept apart
rationale: This follows because a sentence "a and b or c" has two meanings, and the statement must have one.
formula: all f: Series | f in AndInOr implies f in KeepsAndApart
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: a rule keeps its then before a time phrase
rationale: This follows because "when this, then now or at a later moment, that" reads better than two commas in a row.
formula: all f: Series | (f in OneLineRule and f not in TimeFirst and f in TimeSecond) implies f in KeepsThen
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: a rule drops its then before anything else
rationale: This follows because a "then" after every "when" fills the one-line sentence with words that add nothing.
formula: all f: Series | (f in OneLineRule and f not in TimeFirst and f not in TimeSecond) implies f in DropsThen
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: a rule whose first side begins with a time phrase puts its then on a line of its own
rationale: This follows because on one line, the reader would have to guess whether the time phrase covers the second side too.
formula: all f: Series | f in TimeFirst implies f in ThenOwnLine
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: a rule with a list for a side puts its then on a line of its own
rationale: This follows because a rule whose side is a list cannot fit on a line, and "then" tells the reader where the second side starts.
formula: all f: Series | (f in Rule and f not in OneLineRule) implies f in ThenOwnLine
parents: a formula is said without loss

claim: disposing an owner runs its cleanups
formula:
always all o: Owner, c: Cleanup |
  (dispose[o] and c in Registered and c.on = o and c not in Ran) implies eventually c in Ran

claim: dispose runs once
formula:
(always no c: Cleanup, o: Owner | runByCall[c, o])
and
(always no o: Owner | throwByCall[o])

claim: owner cleanups run newest first and in isolation
formula:
(always all o: Owner, c, d: Cleanup |
  (dispose[o] and c + d in Registered - Ran and c.on = o and d.on = o and c->d in Clock.older)
  implies ((not runNow[c]) until runNow[d]))
and
(always all o: Owner, c: Failing |
  (runNow[c] and c.on = o and o in Disposed) implies always o not in Stopped)

claim: a disposed owner cannot be entered
formula: always all o: Owner | (enter[o] and o in Disposed) implies some Throwing'

claim: an owner disposes its sub owners before its own cleanups
formula:
(always all o, k: Owner, c: Cleanup |
  (dispose[o] and k.parent = o and k not in Disposed and c in Registered - Ran and c.on = o)
  implies ((not runNow[c]) until dispose[k]))
and
(always all o, j, k: Owner |
  (dispose[o] and j.parent = o and k.parent = o and j->k in Birth.order and j not in Disposed and k not in Disposed)
  implies ((not dispose[j]) until dispose[k]))

claim: a throwing owner cleanup is reported
formula:
(always all o: Owner, c: Failing |
  (runNow[c] and c.on = o and o in Disposed) implies always o not in Threw)
and
(always all o, h: Owner, c: Failing |
  (runNow[c] and c.on = o and o in Disposed and o.handler = h) implies eventually c.reached = h)
